topic.title: Git Large File Storage (Git LFS) Support
topic.shortdesc: Web Author works with repositories that use Git Large File Storage (Git LFS).

body.p: When a document references a file that is stored with Git LFS (such as an image or a video), Web Author automatically retrieves the actual file so that it is displayed correctly in the editing area.

Git LFS is a Git extension that keeps large binary files (for example, high-resolution images, PDFs, or videos) outside the main repository and stores only a small text pointer in their place. Without this support, such a reference would appear as a few lines of pointer text instead of the intended file. Web Author recognizes these pointers and resolves them transparently, so you can work with the documents as usual.

This support is available for all the Git hosting integrations (GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket Cloud, Bitbucket Server / Data Center, Azure DevOps, and the generic Git connector). It also works with on-premises editions (such as GitHub Enterprise Server and self-managed GitLab).

ul.li: View referenced media - Images, videos, and other assets stored with Git LFS and referenced from your DITA or XML documents are displayed directly in the editing area, just like regular files.

Open Git LFS documents - If an XML document is stored with Git LFS, it opens with its real content rather than the pointer text on the connectors that load documents through the server (Bitbucket Server / Data Center, Azure DevOps, and the generic Git connector).
For the GitHub, GitLab, and Bitbucket Cloud connectors, a document stored with Git LFS opens with the Git LFS pointer shown (three lines starting with version https://git-lfs.github.com/spec/v1), because these connectors load documents directly in the browser. Media (images and videos) referenced from your documents should display correctly on these connectors. No special configuration is required on your side. If the repository already uses Git LFS, Web Author automatically handles the resolution when you open documents.

section.title: Editing and Uploading Git LFS Files
section.p: Editing or uploading files stored with Git LFS is not supported yet. Git LFS files are meant to be viewed in Web Author, not modified.

If you try to save changes to a Git LFS file, or upload a file over an existing Git LFS file, the operation is stopped and the file remains unchanged. A message similar to the following is displayed: “This file is stored with Git LFS. Editing or uploading Git LFS files is not supported yet.”
This safeguard prevents the large file from being accidentally replaced by the small pointer text, which would corrupt the file in the repository.

section.title: Large Files
section.p: To keep the server responsive, files above a configurable size limit are not downloaded. By default, the limit is 100 MB. If a referenced Git LFS file exceeds this limit, it is not retrieved and the reference remains unresolved (the pointer is kept in place).

section.title: Configuration Options (for Administrators)
section.p: You can adjust the default behavior by setting the following system properties:

row.entry: The maximum size, in bytes, of a Git LFS file that Web Author downloads. Files larger than this value are not retrieved. The default is: 104857600 (100 MB).
Set this option to true to turn off Git LFS resolution entirely. When disabled, Git LFS references are shown as pointer text. The default is: false.

p.note: A server restart is required for changes to these options to take effect.
